content.thinking:
There's a discrepancy between the recorded flag change time of 09:07:00 and the logs showing the flag actually on since 09:02, which lines up with the flag rollout numbers. The Argus mitigation timeline also looks contradictory, but overall the evidence still points strongly to a feature-flag toggle being the cause for monthly-spend-fe.

Even after Argus attempted to switch the flag off at 09:07:26, logs at 09:08 still show flag=on with errors continuing, suggesting the remediation never actually propagated rather than the flag being irrelevant. I'm weighing an alternative theory of a latent bad code path in spend_summary.py, but since there were no deployments in the window, the flag-toggle explanation remains the stronger conclusion.

hypotheses.subject: monthly-spend-feature
hypotheses.summary: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on, and the newly enabled code path in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py raises ZeroDivisionError on account page renders. Error rate jumped from ~1% to ~32% in the exact minute the flag evaluations flipped from all-off to almost-all-on (09:02), with no deploy and no traffic, latency or memory change.

hypotheses.summary: Alternative reading of the same evidence: the mitigation is recorded as having set the flag off (09:07:26, and again undone at 09:10:30) yet every log minute from 09:02 onward still prints monthly-spend-feature=on and the ZeroDivisionError persists - i.e. the flag switch does not actually gate the faulty path, and the defect lives in the released code at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:35.
